ai.description: *Rohanixalus senapatiensis* (Rhacophoridae) is a small tree frog measuring 22–25 mm. It is pale yellowish-brown with a distinct dark brown lateral stripe and translucent, unpigmented belly skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Rohanixalus senapatiensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark brown lateral stripe extending from the snout through the eye to the flank.
ai.habitat: *Rohanixalus senapatiensis* inhabits subtropical evergreen forests in Northeast India, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Rohanixalus senapatiensis is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the vegetation near forest streams and wetlands.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rohanixalus senapatiensis* breeds during the monsoon, depositing clutches of 30–50 eggs in foam nests attached to leaves overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: Rohanixalus senapatiensis is endemic to the state of Manipur in Northeast India, where it inhabits mid-elevation forests within the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Rohanixalus senapatiensis* consists of a series of short, high-pitched pulsed notes, typically heard from vegetation near forest streams.
